paragraphs.text: Seizure ENS-11-01 occurred at Ensenada on 2011-01-06. A nightclub manager in Ensenada reported that port authorities detained a fishing vessel in the harbor and removed several sacks that the manager's customers assumed to be cannabis. The manager later learned from a crew member that the sacks contained undeclared abalone taken out of season and that the vessel's owner was fined and released. The reporting office treats the account as an example of routine fisheries enforcement rather than as a drug seizure.

The manager described the Ensenada waterfront during the period as unusually quiet following a series of searches of fishing vessels that the crews attributed to a new harbor master. The manager stated that panga crews were waiting for the attention to pass before resuming night departures and that several had moved their boats to coves south of the city. The manager had no information on who organized the night departures or on their destination. The manager added that the new harbor master was said to be from outside the state and had refused the customary arrangements, and that crews expected the pressure to ease once a replacement was found. The manager has no information on whether any approach to the harbor master was made.

The reporting office assesses this as background on the harbor environment. The source's access is limited to conversations with crew members who frequent the venue. The source has reported accurately on harbor conditions in the past but has no access to the organization of maritime loads. The account is retained because a change in harbor enforcement may affect the pattern of maritime smuggling reported elsewhere.
